class.name: FellowCloth3D
class.brief_description: FellowEngine: cloth — flags, banners, curtains, awnings, capes — simulated on the CPU in small substeps, blown by the scene's wind, colliding with shapes and the physics world, drawn with motion vectors.
class.description: A rectangle of cloth ([member size], [member resolution]), or a [member source_mesh]'s first surface, simulated by position-based dynamics: its vertices welded by position are the particles, each edge a stretch constraint, the two vertices across each pair of triangles a bending constraint, each free particle tethered to its nearest pinned one (no farther along the cloth than at rest times [member tether_slack]). [member pin_mode] says which particles follow the node rather than the simulation: an edge, corners, or the source mesh's vertices whose colour's red is 0.5 or more. The simulation runs in world space, in fixed substeps ([member substep_rate]; [member iterations] passes over the stretch constraints each); pinned particles follow the node between the frames' transforms, the rest swing with inertia. The air: the active [FellowWind3D]'s velocity where the cloth is (with its gusts) times [member wind_scale], plus [member wind], with [member turbulence], pushes each triangle along its normal ([member drag]) and across it ([member lift]) in proportion to the air's speed against the triangle's — a flag streams and flaps. Collisions: the particles, [member thickness] from their surface, are kept out of spheres, capsules, boxes, cylinders, planes and height maps — the shapes in [member colliders] (a [CollisionShape3D] or every shape of a [CollisionObject3D], followed as they move: a character's body), and with [member collide_with_world] the physics world's bodies under the cloth on [member collision_mask] (convex and concave shapes are not collided with), with [member friction]. Every cloth of a frame is simulated at once on the [WorkerThreadPool] after the game's processing ([member Node.process_priority] 100), and drawn as a mesh with one blend shape: its vertices are written each frame through the instance's own buffers, swapped every frame, so that its motion vectors (TAA, FSR) follow the cloth. Past [member lod_distance] from the camera a cloth takes half the substeps; past [member simulation_distance] it is carried with the node without simulating. In the editor it simulates while the 3D editor's Animate toggle is on. See [code]docs/decisions/0181-cloth.md[/code].

method.name: apply_impulse
method.description: Adds [param impulse] (N·s, global) to the free particles within [param radius] of [param position], more near it: a shot through a flag, a character brushing past.

method.name: get_global_stats
method.description: Every cloth's work since [method reset_global_stats]: [code]frames[/code], [code]simulations[/code], [code]substeps[/code], [code]particles[/code] (simulated, summed over frames), [code]simulate_usec[/code] (the worker threads' time, summed), [code]frame_usec[/code] (the main thread's: preparing, waiting, uploading; the debugger's "FellowEngine/Cloth time"), [code]skipped[/code] (frames of cloths past [member simulation_distance]).

method.name: get_particle_count
method.description: The particles: the cloth's vertices welded by position.

method.name: get_stats
method.description: This cloth's [code]particles[/code], [code]triangles[/code], [code]stretch_constraints[/code], [code]bend_constraints[/code], [code]tethers[/code], the last frame's [code]substeps[/code], [code skip-lint]colliders[/code], [code]simulate_usec[/code], [code skip-lint]wind[/code], whether it was past [member lod_distance] ([code]lod[/code]) or [member simulation_distance] ([code]far[/code]), the pinned particles on bones ([code]bone_pins[/code], [member skeleton_path]), and its tears: [code]torn_edges[/code], [code]triangles_all[/code] (as built; [code]triangles[/code] are those left), [code]loose_particles[/code] (of no triangle left).

method.name: get_torn_edge_count
method.description: The edges gone since the cloth was built or [method reset]: broken by [method tear] or [member tear_strain], or left without a triangle.

method.name: is_particle_pinned
method.description: Whether the particle follows the node.

method.name: reset
method.description: The cloth at rest where the node is now (it also resets itself when the node moves more than 5 m in a frame), whole again if it was torn.

method.name: reset_global_stats
method.description: Sets the counters of [method get_global_stats] to zero.

method.name: set_particle_pinned
method.description: Pins a particle where it is now (it follows the node from there), or lets it go (a rope cut, a curtain torn from its rail).

method.name: tear
method.description: Breaks every edge of the cloth passing within [param radius] of [param position] (global): a shot through a flag, a blade's cut (a line of calls along it). The triangles on a broken edge go (a hole: not drawn, no wind on them), with every edge left without a triangle and every bending constraint across one; a particle of no triangle left stays where it is. The tethers are found again along what is left: a part cut from every pin falls free. Emits [signal torn] and returns the edges broken. [method reset] makes the cloth whole again.

members.member: How much the cloth resists folding, 0 to 1 (a substep's share of the bending constraints' error corrected).
Collides with the physics world's bodies overlapping the cloth (one query a frame, the shapes' types listed in the description).
Shapes collided with: [CollisionShape3D]s, or [CollisionObject3D]s (all their shapes); a character's body, a pole.
The physics layers [member collide_with_world] sees.
The particles' velocity lost a second, as a fraction.
The air's push along each triangle's normal (a drag coefficient).
How much a particle touching a collider is held back along its surface, 0 to 1.
The project's gravity, scaled.
Passes over the stretch constraints a substep (more: less stretch, more time).
The air's push across each triangle, as it meets it at an angle (what makes a flag flap).
Past this distance from the camera the cloth takes half the substeps (0: always all).
The fabric's mass per square meter (a flag 0.1-0.3, canvas 0.3-0.6).
The cloth's material; without one, a two-sided light grey one.
The most substeps a frame: a slower frame simulates less than its time rather than ever more work.
The bones the pinned particles may follow ([member skeleton_path]): each is bound to the nearest of them (empty: any bone).
The particles that follow the node.
The generated rectangle's cells along its longer side.
Off: the cloth stays as it is.
Past this distance from the camera the cloth is carried with the node without simulating (0: always simulated).
The generated rectangle (without a [member source_mesh]): from the node's origin, [code]x[/code] meters along +X and [code]y[/code] meters down, facing +Z.

A [Skeleton3D] the pinned particles follow instead of the node (milestone 76): when the cloth is built or reset, each pinned particle is bound to the nearest of [member pin_bones] (the segment from the bone to its first child, as the skeleton is posed then) and keeps its place in that bone's space, interpolated between the frames' poses over the substeps — a cape on the shoulders turns with the chest, a skirt on the hips with them. Put capsules on the bones ([BoneAttachment3D]s with [CollisionShape3D]s) in [member colliders] for the body.
A mesh to simulate instead of the rectangle: its first surface's triangles (vertices at the same position are one particle).
How much the cloth resists stretching, 0 to 1 (1: as little as the substeps allow).
Substeps a second (480: 8 a frame at 60 fps).

An edge stretched by more than this fraction of its length at rest breaks (0.5: half again as long), as [method tear] breaks it — a sheet held at its corners that something goes through tears there, and the tear runs on while it is pulled. Checked once a frame after the substeps; 0: never. See [code]docs/decisions/0220-cloth-tearing.md[/code].
How much farther than at rest (along the cloth) a particle may be from its nearest pin, as a factor (0: no tethers).
The particles' distance from a collider's surface.
Variation of the wind over the cloth and time, as a fraction of its speed.
Wind added to the [FellowWind3D]'s (global, m/s).
The [FellowWind3D]'s wind, scaled.

signal.name: torn
signal.description: Edges broke: by [method tear] (at once), or stretched past [member tear_strain] (after the frame's simulation). [param position] is the broken edges' mean middle (global), [param edges] how many broke.

constants.constant: Nothing pinned: the cloth falls (a sheet onto furniture).
The particles of the highest edge (local +Y): a curtain, a banner.
The particles of the left edge (local −X): a flag on a pole.
The two top corners (local XY): a sheet hung by its corners, a cape.
The four corners (local XY): an awning, a tent's fly.
The source mesh's vertices whose colour's red is 0.5 or more.
